title: The AI Coding Workflow That Actually Ships: Spec → Plan → Execute → Verify
summary: The developers who ship most with AI write specs, not just prompts. Here's the 4-phase workflow that senior developers use in 2026 — and the anti-patterns that break it.
body_markdown:
Before touching code, write a spec. One page maximum.


It needs four things: the problem statement, the constraints (what technologies, what NOT to build), the success criteria (how you'll know it worked), and any known pitfalls.


The spec doesn't need to be a PRD. It needs to be unambiguous. If you can't state the success criteria in two sentences, the AI will fill in gaps with plausible-sounding guesses — none of which you asked for.


In practice, put this in a` SPEC.md` in your project root. Or in your` CLAUDE.md` for persistent context. Claude Code reads` CLAUDE.md` at the start of every session — it's the right place for project-level constraints that should survive context resets.


One pattern Google's Addy Osmani describes in his[2026 coding workflow guide](https://addyosmani.com/blog/ai-coding-workflow/) : "I'll describe the idea and ask the LLM to iteratively ask me questions until we've fleshed out requirements and edge cases." The AI helps draft the spec details; you refine and approve. It's like doing a "waterfall in 15 minutes" — quick structured planning that makes the execution far cleaner.
